statement_record.book: For functors F, G : C -> D, a natural transformation alpha : F => G is a family of arrows alpha_c : Fc -> Gc in D, one per object c of C (its components), such that for every f : c -> c' in C the naturality square commutes: alpha_{c'} . Ff = Gf . alpha_c.
statement_record.intree: Class Transform := { transform {x} : F x ~> G x; naturality {x y} (f : x ~> y) : fmap[G] f ∘ transform ≈ transform ∘ fmap[F] f; naturality_sym {x y} (f : x ~> y) : transform ∘ fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[G] f ∘ transform }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The component family is the implicitly-quantified field `transform {x}` and the naturality square is stated with ≈ on the D-hom-setoid instead of =, the library's faithful setoid rephrasing. The extra field naturality_sym is the mirrored orientation of the SAME equation, carried for definitional duality (C^op^op = C on the nose) and proven redundant in-tree by the smart constructor Build_Transform' (line 129), which derives it from naturality alone — so it adds no content beyond Riehl's definition.

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem Functor_Setoid_Nat_Iso `(F : C ⟶ D) (G : C ⟶ D) : F ≅[Fun] G  ↔  F ≈ G.   (* forward direction constructs, from an isomorphism in the functor category, the family (iso : ∀ x : C, F x ≅ G x); backward direction assembles such a family into a natural isomorphism *)

Program Instance Functor_Setoid {C D : Category} : Setoid (C ⟶ D) := { equiv := fun F G => { iso : ∀ x : C, F x ≅ G x & ∀ (x y : C) (f : x ~> y), fmap[F] f ≈ from (iso y) ∘ fmap[G] f ∘ to (iso x) } }.

statement_record.book: A natural isomorphism is a natural transformation alpha : F => G every component of which is an isomorphism in the target category; written alpha : F ≅ G.
statement_record.intree: F ≅[Fun] G (an Isomorphism in the functor category [C, D], whose to/from are Transforms with two-sided inverse composites), characterized by Functor_Setoid_Nat_Iso : F ≅[Fun] G ↔ F ≈ G, where F ≈ G unfolds to { iso : ∀ x : C, F x ≅ G x & ∀ x y (f : x ~> y), fmap[F] f ≈ from (iso y) ∘ fmap[G] f ∘ to (iso x) }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with the componentwise characterization proven rather than taken as the definition. Riehl DEFINES a natural isomorphism as a componentwise-invertible natural transformation; the library takes the invertible 2-cell F ≅[Fun] G as primitive and proves (Functor_Setoid_Nat_Iso, both directions, Defined) that it is equivalent to a family of component isomorphisms F x ≅ G x satisfying naturality — i.e. Riehl's definition is recovered as a theorem, with iso_equiv/equiv_iso (l.305/308) as the standalone conversions. No extra hypotheses; the naturality condition is stated in the conjugated form fmap[F] f ≈ from(iso y) ∘ fmap[G] f ∘ to(iso x), equivalent to the naturality square by invertibility of the components.

statement_record.book: Seven worked examples/non-examples of naturality: (i) ev_V : V -> V** is natural on Vect_k; (ii) the identity and single-dual functors on fin-dim vector spaces are NOT naturally isomorphic; (iii) eta_A(a) = {a} : id_Set => P is natural; (iv) a natural transformation between X, Y : BG -> C is exactly a G-equivariant morphism; (v) O and C : Top^op -> Set are naturally isomorphic by complementation; (vi) (-)^op : Group -> Group is naturally isomorphic to the identity via inversion; (vii) the only natural transformation from the identity to V |-> V ⊗ V on Vect_k is the zero family — likewise for Hilbert spaces, the 'no cloning theorem'.
statement_record.intree: no_cloning : @braid C _ x x ≈ id[(x ⨂ x)%object], under `{R : @RelevanceMonoidal C} (a diagonal ∆ with diagonal_natural, diagonal_unit, diagonal_braid2, braid_diagonal) and `{CC : @CompactClosed C ...}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker and reformulated. Only clause (vii)'s content has an in-tree counterpart, and in Abramsky's abstract form (arXiv:0910.2401 §4, Theorem 11 second step) rather than Riehl's: the library assumes a NATURAL monoidal cocommutative diagonal in a compact closed category and derives a degeneracy (braid ≈ id, whence every endomorphism is a scalar), whereas Riehl COMPUTES on Vect_k that the only natural family Id ⟹ (-)⊗(-) is the zero family. Both are no-go results about a natural copying map, but neither statement implies the other as written, and the in-tree one carries the extra compact-closed hypothesis. Clauses (i)-(vi) have no counterpart at all.
